title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates who can report and treats sending report data to Microsoft as unconditional, despite documented mailbox prerequisites and destination settings. It also omits a section from the Defender settings path and incorrectly says Microsoft has not confirmed that meeting reports use the documented reporting destinations.

claims.claim: Learn lists iOS and Android reporting as messages only, unlike the roadmap platform list.
claims.quote:
The Microsoft Teams app for iOS/iPadOS: Version 7.15 or later (messages only).
- The Microsoft Teams app for Android: Version 1416/1.0.0.2025153104 or later (messages only).

claims.claim: Every user on a supported client can submit a report from the first meeting after rollout.
claims.quote: User reporting in Teams is supported only for users with an online Teams mailbox. The reporting mailbox configured in **Teams user reported settings** must also be an Exchange Online mailbox. On-premises mailboxes aren't supported in either scenario.
claims.fix: Replace 'Every user on a supported client' with 'Eligible users on supported clients, with an online Teams mailbox and reporting enabled'. Add the online-mailbox prerequisite to Scope, retain the documented licence qualification, and qualify the impact rationale accordingly.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice says administrators can review meeting reports in Defender and in Teams admin center Protection reports.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to review and investigate reported meetings through the Microsoft Defender portal and the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Submitting a report copies meeting and participant metadata to Microsoft for algorithm review without a destination qualification.
claims.quote: If you select **Send the reported items to** > **My reporting mailbox only**, reported items don't go to Microsoft for analysis unless an admin manually submits the item
claims.fix: Say 'When a report is sent to Microsoft, meeting and participant metadata is copied for algorithm review.' Explain the Microsoft only, Microsoft and my reporting mailbox, and My reporting mailbox only destinations. Apply the qualification in Why it matters and the risk rationale.

claims.claim: Microsoft personnel might review submitted meeting and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items.
claims.quote: Microsoft personnel might read submitted messages and files and review submitted call, meeting, and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Content submitted to Microsoft is stored in data centres in the USA.
claims.quote: Submitted content is stored in secured, compliance-audited data centers located in the USA and is deleted as soon as it's no longer required.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams is the documented setting that decides whether reports are shared with Microsoft.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" "PowerShell" parameter'; read submissions-teams and end-user-reporting-teams-meeting. These identify monitoring and a separate reporting experience, but do not identify this toggle as the destination selector.
claims.fix: Describe Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams as controlling monitoring and correct display on User reported. Describe sharing using the documented Reported item destinations > Send the reported items to setting at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams#what-happens-after-a-user-reports-items-from-teams, and add its control row.

claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: The complete meeting-reporting licensing model is not yet published, so the model is unknown.

claims.quote: User reporting of calls, meetings, and messages in Teams is not supported in U.S. Government organizations (Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD).

claims.quote: If user reporting of messages, calls, or meetings is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported items to show up correctly on the **User reported** tab on the **Submissions** page.

claims.claim: The Teams reporting switch controls user availability, and Defender monitoring is irrelevant when the applicable Teams switch is off.
claims.quote: When the applicable setting is turned off, users can't report those items within Teams, so the corresponding setting in the Microsoft Defender portal is irrelevant.

claims.claim: Learn gives a policy or settings page controlling meeting reporting, followed by Allow users to report meetings, in Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, open the policy or settings page that controls reporting for Teams meetings.
3. Select the **Allow users to report meetings** policy.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the Teams meeting-reporting availability policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting security concern reporting PowerShell Graph API Allow users report meetings Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy'; opened meeting-reporting and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, searched its full reference for report, concern and security; no corresponding parameter or API found.

claims.claim: The Defender path goes directly from Teams user reported settings to Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: On the **Teams user reported settings** page, go to the **Microsoft Teams** section for the **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and the rendered row to 'Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Microsoft Teams > Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams'. The missing Microsoft Teams section is documented in the cited page.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the specific Defender monitoring toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" "PowerShell" parameter'; read submissions-teams and searched Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy for Teams, chat and monitor. Found destination parameters, but no parameter identified as the monitoring-toggle equivalent.

claims.claim: Learn names Allow users to report meetings but supplies no precise navigation page or assignment scope.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting security concern reporting PowerShell Graph API Allow users report meetings Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy'; read end-user-reporting-teams-meeting and submissions-teams. The former says 'policy or settings page' and neither specifies the meeting policy's assignment scope.

claims.claim: Learn documents Report a security concern within messaging-policy configuration for message reporting.
claims.quote: On the selected tab (**Global (Org-wide) default settings** or **Custom policies for users & groups**), go to the **Messaging** section and select **Messaging**.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy configures reported Teams item destinations.
claims.quote:
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy `
    -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageAddresses "securityadmin@contoso.com"

claims.claim: Microsoft does not confirm meeting coverage for the documented Teams reported-item destination configuration.
claims.quote: When users report Teams messages or calls or report meetings or meeting participants as malicious or non malicious, the reported items are sent to Microsoft and/or the reporting mailbox as defined by the Teams user reported settings in Defender for Office 365.
claims.fix: Replace the meeting-coverage disclaimer with the SecOps guide's explicit statement that meeting and participant reports use Teams user reported destinations. Explain that submissions-teams documents Exchange Online PowerShell for those destinations, while the cmdlet reference still describes its ReportChatMessage parameters in terms of messages and calls.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy documents no separate meeting-security-reporting parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting security concern reporting PowerShell Graph API Allow users report meetings Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy'; opened the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference and searched its full text for report, concern and security; found attendance reporting, not security-concern reporting.

claims.claim: No Graph endpoint for meeting security reports was found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Teams meeting user reported security concern submissions API'; read returned Teams reporting passages and opened submissions-teams, end-user-reporting-teams-meeting and the SecOps guide; no relevant Graph endpoint documented.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends updating security awareness training and incident-response documentation.
claims.quote: Update security awareness training, incident response documentation, and internal guidance as needed.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to review reported-call alert policies, but the controls table has no alert-policy row.
claims.quote: Review the alert policies for reported calls, which also cover reported meetings and participants, so the right team receives them. | The four control rows cover reporting availability, monitoring, Defender submissions and Teams reports, not alert-policy configuration.
claims.fix: Add a control row for the reported-call security-risk and not-security-risk alert policies that also cover meetings. Research its management UI and automation separately; use the existing SecOps and submissions-teams sources to establish meeting applicability.
